records.text: Owens characterized Pete Hegseth’s recent proposal as executing the Fort Hood shooter and livestreaming it.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Liars, right? By the way, in case you were following the, the administration, and you know Pete Hegseth, who tries to pretend to be tough, he just kind of, just always jogging with people in the military. I'll jog with you at 5 a.m. Never mind, I'm going to send you to die for Israel, right? Well, one of his recent tough guy things was, we are going to be executing the Fort Hood shooter and we're going to live stream it. What?

records.text: Owens opposed turning an execution into a public livestream, distinguishing support for a death sentence for the Fort Hood shooter from wanting to watch him die, and rejected framing the question as theological because the country is not a theocracy.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: What are we even speaking about right now? We used to be a civilized society and debate the death penalty in general, like do you support death penalty? ... Why you support it? Why you don't support it? Now we are suddenly at this radical point where people are trying to say it is totally legitimate for us to just live stream the death. Like that's a totally normal thing to want to watch someone die. ... The Fort Hood shooter, by the way, obviously not an innocent person. He murdered a lot of people. And you can say, I believe that he should be put to death. ... If people are trying to make theological arguments, oh, well, this is what, guys, we don't live in a theocracy.

records.text: Owens described a Trump Truth Social post as stopping a publicly livestreamed execution of Nidal Malik Hasan while allowing immediate victims’ families to witness an execution if they wished. Her lead-in also says Hasan “would not be executed”; the transcript’s account is internally inconsistent on cancellation of the execution itself.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And you do not want to empower the Epstein class to go around and commit executions based on what they deem to be worthy of live streaming executions. It's so dark and Epstein coded, and it made me sick when there was even a debate. But yes, to tell you quickly, Trump (Donald Trump) did issue a truth social post where where he established that Nidal Malik Hasan, who was the former U.S. Army major turned traitor, ... would not be executed. It would not be live streamed. And he wrote a long post. He said he was scum, but there are well-meaning people who would rather not watch him die. Also, he's paraplegic. I don't know how that's going to play on TV. ... Anyway, he did acknowledge in his truth social post, Donald Trump said that the execution can be viewed by people in the immediate family of the victims if they so choose. ... because they deserve to witness it if they want to.
